summary: Completed 4,207,129 new physical training hands across four two-seed LR branches and 262,144 internal evaluation executions on 32,768 unique paired decks. Independent terminal review passed. Final half-minus-full was +8.6078 bb/100 in Seed1 and -10.9086 in Seed3, both nominal intervals crossing zero. Seed3 half-rate early improvement reversed: its parent-relative stage2-minus-stage1 change was -43.6969 [-67.0911,-20.3027]. No Slumbot or final-qualification hands were generated.
conclusion: Reducing the actual Adam LR halved mean PPO update KL and reduced early stops, but did not establish reproducible poker improvement or preservation. Original-rate endpoints were -2.3225 and -9.5087 bb/100 versus their fixed parents; half-rate endpoints were +6.2853 and -20.4172. The severe preregistered broad-collapse gate was false in both seeds, yet the curve does not support automatic larger allocation under the unchanged recipe. This is adverse/inconclusive internal scaling evidence, not proof that all full-representation learning fails at paper scale. Full-trainable scope still excludes direct preflop-actor and critic-v2 gradients to the shared representation. That contract observation is not a causal explanation of the losses.
decision: Do not select a learning-rate winner or automatically launch 4M/16M/paper-scale training. Retain both frozen final LR arms and both seeds. Before changing another training mechanism, calibrate these previously externally untested full-representation endpoints against Slumbot using a prospectively fixed 80k development allocation: all four policies receive 20k new hands each, regardless of interim scores. Existing internal/external ranking disagreement makes direct external calibration more decision-relevant than another proxy-only diagnostic or blindly extending this LR comparison.
next_step: Register and qualify a four-policy frozen external development calibration in a new experiment, reusing the established journaled CPU-greedy physical-v6/legacy-v4 bridge and audit/statistics machinery. Freeze all four current stage2 checkpoint hashes, runtime, distinct session IDs/policy seeds, balanced scheduling, 8x2500 hands per policy, no score-based stopping/extension/retry, raw/session uncertainty and multiplicity handling before any network request. Verify no live poker-owner overlap. After all 80k hands and evidence checks, assess external direction, severity and internal/external agreement before choosing further scale or a single-change general training control. A preflop actor-to-representation gradient-route control remains a hypothesis, not an adopted fix. No Slumbot labels/action rules, no final qualification credit, and no new training in that calibration.
